decisionRule: Accept only one-time full-sentence comparisons/images without a bounded reusable target. Reject an exclusion when an ordinary reusable expression, earlier-owner route, or repeat requires further editorial treatment. Rejection retains hold, not alias or lesson approval.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The teams worked like isolated islands before the merger.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Separate groups with little connection; an island metaphor.
rows.reason: The teams are explicitly likened to isolated islands before a merger. This whole island simile is tailored to that organisational separation; it supplies no fixed target beyond the comparison.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A business model that chases profit and forgets people will lose trust.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Prioritises money while neglecting human effects; a pursuit personification.
rows.reason: “Chases profit” is a reusable business-priority collocation, and “forgets people” supplies its ethical contrast. The complete warning is composed, but excluding the source would discard a plausible bounded chase-profit target; retain hold pending course-value review.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The markets now operate on the same circuit.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A shared system that transmits effects rapidly; an electrical metaphor.
rows.reason: Markets operating on the same circuit borrows an electrical network image without a literal circuit. “Same circuit” alone lacks a stable market sense, so this sentence is a one-time explanatory comparison.

rows.exactExpression: a mirror and a mood board rolled into one
rows.exactSourceSentence: The magazine felt like a mirror and a mood board rolled into one.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Something that reflects identity and inspires taste at once; paired object metaphors.
rows.reason: “A mirror and a mood board rolled into one” contains the established combination expression taught by earlier owner1181 “all rolled into one / roll … into one”. The two nouns are source-specific, but the reusable target merits a bounded owner variant check before exclusion.

rows.exactExpression: at the speed of a swipe
rows.exactSourceSentence: New trends now spread at the speed of a swipe.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Very quickly in a phone-driven culture; a contemporary speed image.
rows.reason: “At the speed of a swipe” is coined for phone-driven trend spread. The reusable speed frame is broad, but this full swipe comparison has no stable independent target; do not treat this as excluding other “at the speed of” uses.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Freedom should not mean crashing into other people.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Interfering with others' rights or safety; a collision metaphor.
rows.reason: Freedom crashing into other people is a one-time collision image for infringing others’ rights. Literal crash and general disagreement uses would not preserve this source-specific ethical claim.

rows.exactExpression: city runs on millions of small acts of trust
rows.exactSourceSentence: A city runs on millions of small acts of trust.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Urban life depends on countless reliable interactions; a machine metaphor.
rows.reason: “Runs on” is a reusable dependency construction: a city depends on everyday acts of trust. Earlier owner1651 “do not run on good intentions alone” teaches practical inputs to a service; sense and grammar need comparison before excluding this source.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A household is a small shared world.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A family as a close social environment; a world metaphor.
rows.reason: “A household is a small shared world” is a whole-family-as-world analogy. Neither “small world” nor “shared world” alone preserves the source’s rule/community point as a settled target.

rows.exactExpression: lighting the torch and handing it on
rows.exactSourceSentence: Good teaching is like lighting the torch and handing it on.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Passing knowledge and inspiration to the next generation; a torch metaphor.
rows.reason: The explicit teaching/torch simile contains a recognisable pass-the-torch/hand-on-the-torch succession idea. The source wording is adapted, but the transferable hand-on construction and owner boundary must be checked before one-off exclusion.

rows.exactExpression: teaching passes on the map, but research redraws it
rows.exactSourceSentence: At the seminar, she said teaching passes on the map, but research redraws it over time.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Teaching transmits knowledge while research changes it; an extended map metaphor.
rows.reason: Teaching passing on a map while research redraws it is a composed two-part comparison; neither half alone teaches the source’s transmission-versus-discovery claim.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Without research, we may offer yesterday's answers to tomorrow's questions.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Outdated knowledge applied to new problems; a time contrast.
rows.reason: Yesterday’s answers to tomorrow’s questions is a crafted temporal antithesis for outdated research. Its whole wording, not a stable idiom, carries the one-time argument.

rows.exactExpression: one of the engines that keeps the world moving forward
rows.exactSourceSentence: Research is one of the engines that keeps the world moving forward.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: A force driving social progress; a vehicle metaphor.
rows.reason: “An engine that keeps … moving forward” is reusable driving-force imagery. Earlier owner526 teaches an engine keeping a business moving; owner2400 matches only “keeps … moving” with different operational sense. A bounded engine-owner comparison is required before exclusion.

rows.exactExpression: every powerful tool casts a shadow
rows.exactSourceSentence: Every powerful tool casts a shadow when used carelessly.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Major benefits may have harmful side effects; a shadow metaphor.
rows.reason: “Casts a shadow” is a reusable negative-consequence metaphor. Earlier “cast a long shadow” owner2513 adds persistence not stated here, so direct alias is unsafe; keep the source for distinct-sense/owner review rather than exclude.

rows.exactExpression: every powerful tool casts a shadow
rows.exactSourceSentence: Every powerful tool casts a shadow when used carelessly.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: Major benefits may have harmful side effects; a shadow metaphor.
rows.reason: This repeats 3731’s exact tool/shadow sentence. Because 3731 is retained for a reusable “casts a shadow” owner check, its duplicate must follow the same eventual disposition, not be excluded separately.

rows.exactExpression: in the cracks of daily life
rows.exactSourceSentence: People now buy groceries in the cracks of daily life.
rows.sourceMeaningAndReason: In brief spare moments within a busy routine; a crack metaphor.
rows.reason: Buying groceries “in the cracks of daily life” is an image for spare moments in a schedule. The full cracks-of-life locative phrase is tailored to this shopping example and not a stable idiom.
